learning_outcomes.text: After participating in the module events, students are able to transfer theoretical approaches to heat transfer to practical applications.
Students can describe the principles of energy conservation in heat transfer and apply them to technical systems.
Students understand the mathematical foundations of heat conduction and can solve the heat conduction equation for simple, one-dimensional problems.
Students can numerically determine the convective heat transfer coefficient for free and forced convection.
Students are able to explain the fundamentals of heat transfer by radiation, analyze influencing factors, and calculate radiation exchange problems.
Students can calculate unsteady heat transfer processes such as the heating and cooling of bodies.
Students know the thermodynamic principles of heat exchangers and can use them for analysis and optimization.
Students can design heat exchangers and heat storage units using the NTU method, apply iterative calculation methods, and evaluate pressure losses.
Students understand the functioning of heat storage units and are able to design them for specific applications.
Students are able to perform heating load calculations and apply them to building systems.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of heat conduction (heat conduction equation, 1-dimensional solution)
Fundamentals of convective heat transfer (determination of the convective heat transfer coefficient for free and forced convection)
Fundamentals of heat transfer by radiation (influencing factors, irradiation factor, radiation exchange between multiple bodies)
Unsteady heat transfer phenomena (heating and cooling of bodies)
Fundamentals of thermodynamics of heat exchangers
Selection and design of heat exchangers (NTU method, iterative methods, pressure drop calculation)
Heat storage units and their design
Systems with heat exchangers and heat storage units: e.g., PCM storage in combination with solar thermal and heat pump
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
